newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen erring down, peso stable.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen erring down, peso stable.

text.p: --Mexico stocks seen lower on Wall Street jitters
--Peso likely stable on high domestic rates
--Cetes overnight rate seen down, speculation eases

Dealers saw stocks opening with mild downside potential on Monday, with Friday's international jitters continuing on an early slide in the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, down 13/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
"We expect a typically slow Monday start, with dealers selling a little on Wall Street nerves," one desk trader said.
Technical analysts placed support at 5,035 points on the IPC scale, down from Friday's close of 5,067.03.
Traders expected the peso to open stable with high money market yields offsetting the adverse effect of higher yields on the U.S. long bond.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.8250/7.8450 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.8325/7.8370 per dollar, compared to Friday's close of 7.8350/7.8400.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen easing down from Friday's close of 24.25 percent which was reached after late market ,speculation.
